title: Structure updates and internal documentation improvements
description: This PR mostly merges how nodes are defined. Previously node definitions were split into "information" and "rendering" parts. This was due to the mono repo previously having a separate package for node info definitions. The problem is this was super confusing and only for historical reasons. So after an unreasonably large set of diffs, the info and rendering are all declared in a single large object. Because this object is large and relatively nuanced, there is now a readme file explaining what goes into it in the `ui_node_definitions` directory.

title: input/output ID leaked value bug
description:
Due to additional logic added to the input for the ID property for inputs and outputs, when you would switch between two inputs or outputs of the same type (e.g. `checkboxGroup`) then you would see the _previously_ selected input's ID in place of the current ones. See #243.

This PR fixes that bug by better structuring the hook logic in the `InputId` component and also adds an e2e test for the scenario to avoid future regressions.

title: 0.5.1 Release
description: Bump version number and update News.md

title: 190 support nav panel within apps using the page navbar template
description: This PR adds support for the newer `nav_panel` function to make tabs. The old `tabPanel()` support has been moved into an alias for `nav_panel()` which will result in an automatic updating of code to `nav_panel()`.

title: Website demo fixes
description:
- Make the live demo embed look better on short screens
- Fix live-demo not being able to go past template-chooser screen due to missing `tree-sitter.wasm` bundle

title: Delete bound output code if deleting element
description: Previously if you deleted an output like a plot that had some render code in the server associated with it, that server code would be left in the server without and bindings. This PR adds logic to detect when deleting a node is about to create this orphaned output code and asks if the user wants to delete that code or leave it. This really helps in the situation where you start with a template that has pre-defined output code that you almost definitely don't want.

title: Id syncing
description: This PR adds the feature of synced input and output IDs. Now if you have existing server code using an input or output, and you change that input or outputs id now the server code referencing that input id will update so your app doesnt break.  E.g. you change a slider's id from `"my_slider"` to `"num_rows"`, now server code that references `input$my_slider` will be updated to `input$num_rows`.

title: Fix server selection for R backend
description: Fixes bug from #210 where server code selection in RStudio was not working.

title: Remove multifile support
description:
This PR removes the support for multifile apps. 

The tradeoff here is significantly increased complexity in dealing with apps spread over multiple files. Also, modern shiny practices encourage single-file apps.

title: Smarter ID input
description: This PR adds a new `inputType` for the configuration of UI nodes called `"id"`. This type is similar to the standard string input but it makes sure that inputs arent repeated and don't have spaces in them. Will open up further smart behavior for ids such as auto-changing server code to reflect new id etc..

title: Switch website from pkgdown to astro
description: In an attempt to keep a fast and modern landing page this PR updates from using a pkgdown site to using an astro static site. This allows much easier and less hacky workflows for things like including live demos of the editor in the site.

title: Fix email
description: We no longer use rstudio domains for email.

title: Remove alpha message
description: After Posit Conf 2023 we're finally removing the big scary warning.

title: Beta release
description: Big PR with lots of updates the main being switching to treesitter for parsing on the client

title: Tree-Sitter support
description: This PR swaps out the main parsing engine for R with tree-sitter. This is to bring it up-to-par with python parsing. This also allows the whole system to be faster and run in a greater number of places without the user getting their whole R environment setup.

title: Initial python support
description: This PR (in progress) will add python support to the ui editor with a limited set of components to work from. There are also substantial under-the-hood changes to make the codebase more modular.

title: Add simple python support and modularize codebase
description:
This PR adds very basic (and non-enabled) support for ShinyForPython apps along with a new repo structure where info about the UI nodes is stored in a separate "library" in the main mono-repo so it can be shared across the different backends/clients without needing to bring along the entire react dependency and all the annoying with it. 

The main con of this change is that to add an element to the editor, you now need to add it in two places: 
1. In the `inst/ui-node-definitions/` library for the basic information
2. In the `inst/editor/` library to bind it to a React Component and provide optional render overrides for the settings panels.

title: Code-gen for Shiny-For-Python
description: This PR adds a new language mode for Python that can currently generate code for a small number of components.

title: Misc bug squash
description:
Fixes bug where empty card header and footers would show up in the vscode extension even if they weren't actually present in the card. Was due to the over-optimistic use of the `:has()` selector, which isnt supported in vscode's webview yet. 


It also fixes a nasty bug where, when using the editor from the R function `launch_editor()`, if you refreshed the page the whole app could just vanish. This was caused due to the backend trying to always guarantee that if the user had switched app types from the template viewer that it didn't leave around old files. Unfortunately, this meant that it erased existing files every time the app loaded, which, when a refresh happened, would be the app you were working on...

title: Fix invisible selection outline for valueboxes
description: Bug/issue is caused by the fact that the `--font-color` variable is overridden inside of the value box container to white so that text shows up on the blue background. This override caused the selection outline, which for the value box used that `--font-color` to get a dark outline color, to switch its outline to white, thus making it invisible.

title: Build assets with CI
description: This PR updates how the repo enforces built assets. Previously it used a pre-commit hook that ran `yarn prod` on every commit. Now it will run `yarn prod` and push results.

title: R language separation
description: This PR is mostly type updates and renaming of some internal object properties to make the code less inherently tied to R as the output language

title: Bslib value boxes
description:
This PR adds new {bslib} value boxes to the editor. 
It also has some internal updates to make it easier to create more flexible ui components such as allowing named args to contain other known ui nodes and to pre/post process an elements ui-ast tree

title: Tree navigation with named args
description: Update the `NodePath` type to allow indexing into named arguments instead of only un-named children nodes. This will allow a greater variety of apis to be reflected in the editor. Allowing things like dragging ui nodes into slots that correspond to arguments instead of relying on intermediate representations that treat those types of nodes as fake children.

title: Client error boundaries
description: This PR adds a series of error boundaries around the app to catch errors that occur before they can crash the entire app. They also give a series of options for the user experiencing the error to deal with it, along with one that submits a bug report to github.

title: Drop on grid bug fix
description: Fixes a bug introduced in the cards release where items dragged directly onto the grid that werent gridlayout items or a bslib::card() would not get wrapped in the proper element and thus cause wonky things to happen. Also updates the playwright test for drag-and-drop behavior to catch this kind of regression in the future.

title: Catch failures in parsing and communicate to them to the users
description:
This PR adds better error handling around failures in parsing the shiny app into the format used by the editor. Previously failures could result in a blank screen crash of the editor. Now, these failures will be caught and communicated to the user, allowing them to fix them and move on without needing to completely restart the whole editor. 

Related to #56

title: Make ast serialization more forgiving of calls of declared-in-scope functions
description:
This is a fix for the bug in #148 . 

## Problem
In code to serialize from R code to the general purpose ast the use of `rlang::call_match()` is not able to handle the case where the function itself is not defined for the calling environment that `call_match()` is run. This means declaring a function inside your server function or app script and then calling it would break the serialization. 

## Fix
The fix, in this case, is to just not error when we encounter this situation and pass the non-matched function expression on. This is safe to do because we only need the named arguments separated properly for editable UI code, where any recently declared functions won't fall into this situation anyways.

title: add commas between remotes
description: Closes #146 hopefully

title: Bslib card support
description: This (too large) PR includes support for the new `bslib::card()` function (and the paired `gridlayout::grid_card()`) along with some stability enhancements and bug fixes. (See `news.MD`).

title: Simplify build tooling
description: Switch from home-made esbuild pipeline to vite to simplify config and ensure best-practices for minification etc are being used. Esbuild is still used for the extension backend but just simple node-scripts copied from the vscode extension docs.

title: Server-aware editing in VSCode and static app script generation
description:
Big PR that adds server-aware logic to the VSCode extension (go to output definitions and input references) along with the ability to see a full app script when running in static (or embedded mode). 

Under the hood these changes are driven by a large rewrite of the data structures used to represent an app. Now the client is given full information about the underlying app (both script text and AST) and parses that to render and update the UI. This means a large percentage of the R code has been removed.

title: VSCode extension and keyboard shortcuts
description: This PR has large amounts of low-level changes including a project structure refactor to a monorepo setup. However, the user facing changes amount to a new way of using the editor: as a VSCode extension, and the addition of keyboard shortcuts for deleting elements and undoing/redoing changes.

title: Add playwright test to make sure keyboard shortcuts work properly
description: Also fixes keyboard shortcuts in VSCode extension

Changes:

### Major new features and improvements

title: Css unit info

title: Grid item resizing fixes and simplification
description:
This PR updates the algorithm used for resizing a grid item. It has a few nicities associated with it:
1. It fixes the problem where items that were resized would sometimes not snap to the size they should when they should. This was due to a mistake in the grid-cell position code that caused overlaps which favored expansion and thus made shrinking behave oddly. 
2. Previously we relied on the grid cells components keeping their sizes up-to-date with resize observers and shared reference variables which led to a lot of confusing leakage between the interfaces and potential slowdowns on resize events with large grids. Now we just use computed styles to find just the tract extents needed for resizing on drag start. This greatly simplifies the variables and references that need to be juggled around.
3. Took advantage of being inside the resize codebase to remove some old no-longer-used code such as the drag-to-move logic that is now replaced with simply dropping elements using drag listeners.

title: Fix out-of-place `NULL` return value when exiting ui editor early
description: I had wrapped the `return` call in `invisible()` rather than returning `invisible()`. Now the reason for the early exit is printed and no awkward raw return value is shown.

title: Spin the app preview reload button when it is clicked
description: Helps demonstrate to the user that something actually happened when they clicked. Solves #34.

title: Stop editor on browser close
description:
This PR makes it so the ui editor server interrupts itself if the browser window is closed or inactive. This means the user doesn't have to close the browser tab and then interrupt the R console afterwords to continue using their R console. 

The auto-close behavior can be turned off by setting argument `stop_on_browser_close = FALSE` in `launch_editor()`.

Based on #27

title: Segmented UI parsing
description:
This PR adds the ability for the UI editor to work on single-file apps.
Also adds
- Support for preserving and adding `library()` calls
- De-namespacing function names for cleaner code
- General cleanup of the R code structure

title: Handle unknown args
description:
This PR adds support for unknown arg types. Previously if an argument was not a primative type like a string, number or simple array/list then it _would_ be silently carried around the app and not touched. However, when an arguments is more complicated and is something like an s3 class or other non-trivial object the UI editor would simply complain and say it couldn't handle it and make the user throw it away to use the app. This PR treats these fancy unknown arguments like it does unknown ui children, they are wrapped in the intermediate representation and unwrapped in by the IR parsing/deparsing code with no changes. This means you can now do things like have animation argument classes in your slider input:

```R
ui <- gridlayout::grid_page(
      ...,
      shiny::sliderInput(
        inputId = "bins",
        label = "Number of Bins",
        min = 12L,
        max = 100L,
        value = 30L,
        animate = animationOptions(
          interval = 1000,
          loop = FALSE,
          playButton = "play",
          pauseButton = "pause"
      )
    ),
    ...
   )
```
and (while you wont be able to edit the animation class with the visual editor) you will be able to use the editor just fine on all the supported/known arguments.

title: Function text formatting fix
description: Safari does not support look aheads and look behinds in regexes and fails spectacularly when they exist. This PR removes the use of look aheads and look behinds in the formatting of text for unknown ui functions. Tests are also added so any future work can be easily tested for regressions.

title: Editor round one feedback updates
description:
This update includes:
- Ability to swap grid panels using drag behavior
- Single-element grid_panel that will dump its element into another panel if dragged into it, avoiding orphaned grid panels
- Usability hints like messages for empty grid panels along with options to delete
- Switch to nicer-looking array-based gridlayout layout definitions 
- Switch to new gridlayout grid_panel*() function names
- Custom icons
- Organization in the elements palette by node category
- Auto launching of browser on editor startup
- Ability to restart the background shiny processes from within the UI editor
- Make gridlayout a hard-dependency as it's the only way to build an app currently (https://github.com/rstudio/Shiny-Visual-Editor/issues/14#issue-1212911221)
- Fix of hard-coded websocket address that would cause editor to only work on port `8888` ([065c951](https://github.com/rstudio/Shiny-Visual-Editor/pull/15/commits/065c9519a0896158a000eaac5fe29061728a0ebc)) (https://github.com/rstudio/Shiny-Visual-Editor/issues/14#issuecomment-1106997331)
